### ADM Reports Fourth Quarter and Full-Year 2024 Results; Provides 2025 Guidance

February 4, 2025

Full-Year Reported EPS 2 of $3.65, Adjusted EPS 1,2 of $4.74

Announces Targeted Actions to Deliver $500 - $750 Million in Cost Savings

Announces Increase in Quarterly Dividend

CHICAGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--  ADM (NYSE: ADM) today reported financial results for the fourth quarter and full year ended December 31, 2024.

**Full-Year 2024 Highlights**

*   Net earnings of $1.8 billion, adjusted net earnings 1 of $2.3 billion
*   Earnings per share 2 of $3.65, with adjusted earnings per share 1,2 of $4.74, both down versus the prior year
*   Trailing four-quarter average return on invested capital (ROIC) of 6.7%, trailing four-quarter average adjusted return on invested capital (ROIC)1 of 8.3%

2024 cash flows from operating activities were $2.8 billion, with cash flows from operations before working capital 1,3 of $3.3 billion, as compared to 2023 cash flows from operating activities of $4.5 billion and cash flows from operations before working capital 1,3 of $4.7 billion.

Board Chair and CEO Juan Luciano commented, “With softer market conditions and policy uncertainty around the world going into 2025, we are focused on improving our operational performance, accelerating costs savings, and simplifying our portfolio. As part of that effort, we are announcing targeted actions to deliver $500 – 750 million in cost savings over the next several years. This represents a continuation of ADM’s commitment to drive simplification and better align our resources to deliver long-term sustainable growth.

“We will also maintain our disciplined and balanced approach to capital allocation, including prioritizing selective strategic investments with strong return potential and returning cash to shareholders. In line with this, we are announcing a 2% increase in our quarterly dividend.”

**Fourth Quarter and Full-Year 2024 Results**

**Summary of Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2024**

For the fourth quarter ended December 31, 2024, earnings before income taxes were $667 million, down (9)% versus the prior year quarter. Earnings per share on a GAAP basis were $1.17, up 10% from the prior year quarter, and adjusted earnings per share were $1.14, down (16)% versus the prior year quarter. Total segment operating profit was $1,051 million, down (16)% versus the prior year quarter, and excluded specified items of $(36) million related to gain on sale of assets and lowering of contingency liability reserves.

For the full year, earnings before income taxes were $2.3 billion, down (47)% versus the prior year. Earnings per share on a GAAP basis were $3.65 and adjusted earnings per share were $4.74, both lower versus the prior year. Total segment operating profit was $4.2 billion, down (28)% versus the prior year, and excluded specified items of $480 million primarily related to the Wilmar investment impairment, Nutrition trade name impairments, and gain on asset sales.

**Ag Services and Oilseeds Summary**

AS&O segment operating profit was $644 million during the fourth quarter of 2024, down (32)% compared to the prior year quarter.

The Ag Services subsegment operating profit was 19% higher versus the prior year quarter, due to higher origination volumes and margins in North America, supported by improved river conditions. The subsegment also had benefits from positive timing impacts, as well as higher destination marketing volumes and margins in Global Trade.

The Crushing subsegment operating profit was (46)% lower versus the prior year quarter, as increased industry run rates, higher manufacturing costs, and biofuel and trade policy uncertainty drove lower executed crush margins in North America, partially offset by higher margins and volumes in EMEA. There were immaterial net mark-to-market timing effects during the quarter compared to approximately $35 million of net positive impacts in the prior year quarter. The current quarter also included $52 million of insurance proceeds for the partial settlement of the Decatur East and West claim.

The Refined Products and Other (RPO) subsegment operating profit was (57)% lower versus the prior year quarter, as biofuel and trade policy uncertainty, increased pre-treatment capacity, and higher imports of used cooking oil negatively impacted margins in Europe and North America. Softer demand from food customers in North America negatively impacted refining margins compared to the prior year. During the quarter, there were approximately $50 million of net negative mark-to-market timing effects compared to approximately $5 million of net positive impacts in the prior year quarter.

Equity earnings from the Company’s investment in Wilmar were approximately (20)% lower versus the prior year period.

For the full year, the AS&O segment operating profit was $2.4 billion, (40)% lower compared to 2023.

In the Ag Services subsegment, operating profit was (39)% lower versus the prior year, as slower farmer selling and higher logistics costs related industry take-or-pay commitments negatively impacted the South American origination environment.

In the Crushing subsegment, operating profit was $844 million, (35)% lower versus the prior year, as ample supplies out of South America drove more balanced supply and demand conditions, leading to lower crush margins. For 2024, there were approximately $20 million of net positive mark-to-market timing effects, compared to approximately $185 million of net positive impacts in the prior year. The full year also included $76 million of insurance proceeds for the partial settlement of the Decatur East and West claims related to incidents in 2023.

The RPO subsegment operating profit was $552 million, (58)% lower versus the prior year, as increased pre-treatment capacity at renewable diesel facilities and higher imports of used cooking oil drove significantly lower biodiesel and refining margins. For 2024, there were approximately $195 million of net negative mark-to-market timing effects, compared to approximately $235 million of net positive impacts in the prior year.

Equity earnings from the Company’s investment in Wilmar were $336 million in 2024, approximately 11% higher than the prior year.

**Carbohydrate Solutions Summary**

Carbohydrate Solutions segment operating profit was $319 million during the fourth quarter of 2024, up 3% compared to the prior year quarter.

The Starches & Sweeteners (S&S) subsegment decreased (3)%, versus the prior year quarter, as higher volumes and margins in North America were offset by lower co-product values and margins in EMEA. The current quarter also included $37 million of insurance proceeds related to both the partial settlement of the Decatur East and West insurance claim.

In the Vantage Corn Processor (VCP) subsegment, operating profit increased due to higher ethanol export volumes and improved ethanol margins relative to the prior year quarter.

For the full year, Carbohydrate Solutions segment operating profit was $1.4 billion, flat compared to the prior year. In S&S, strong margins and volumes in North America were offset by weaker domestic ethanol margins, co-product values, and margins in EMEA. In 2024, there were $84 million of insurance proceeds related to the partial settlement of the Decatur East and West claims. In VCP, operating profit declined relative to the prior year, as strong exports volumes were more than offset by lower margins due to higher industry production and inventory levels.

**Nutrition Summary**

Nutrition segment operating profit was $88 million during the fourth quarter of 2024, an increase from the segment operating loss of $(10) million in the prior year quarter.

Human Nutrition subsegment operating profit was $62 million compared to a loss of $(25) million in the prior year quarter. Results were higher due to the lapping of previously disclosed non-recurring negative impacts from the prior year, higher volumes and improved mix, and strong performance by recent M&A, partially offset by higher costs. During the quarter, there were also negative impacts due to higher costs of goods sold associated with the termination of an unfavorable supply agreement. The current quarter also included $46 million of insurance proceeds related to the partial settlement of the Decatur East claim.

In the Animal Nutrition subsegment, operating profit was $26 million, up relative to the prior year quarter, as cost optimization actions and lower input costs supported higher margins.

For the full year, Nutrition segment operating profit was $386 million, (10)% lower versus the prior year.

Human Nutrition subsegment operating profit of $327 million was (22)% lower than the prior year, driven primarily by negative impacts related to unplanned downtime at Decatur East and lower texturants pricing. The full year also included $71 million of insurance proceeds related to the partial settlement of the Decatur East claim.

Animal Nutrition subsegment operating profit of $59 million was higher compared to the prior year as cost optimization efforts and lower input costs supported higher margins.

**Corporate and Other Business Summary**

For the fourth quarter, Other business contributed operating profit of $47 million, down 68% compared to the prior year quarter due to lower Captive insurance results from higher claim losses. ADM Investor Services results decreased on lower interest income.

For the full year, Other business contributed operating profit of $247 million, down 34% compared to the prior year due to lower Captive insurance results from higher claim settlements. Included in claim settlements were partial settlements of $231 million for the Decatur East and West insurance claims of which $133 million was from reinsurers during the fourth quarter.

In Corporate for the fourth quarter, unallocated corporate costs decreased versus the prior year due to $52 million in lower incentive compensation, partially offset by $28 million of increased legal fees.

In Corporate for the full year, unallocated corporate costs increased versus the prior year on higher global technology investments to support digital transformation efforts, $103 million in increased legal fees and $38 million in increased financing costs, partially offset by lower incentive compensation. Other Corporate was favorable compared to last year’s investment valuation losses.

**Outlook 3**

The Company provided guidance for the full year 2025. ADM expects adjusted earnings per share in the range of $4.00 to $4.75 per share 1,2 , reflecting weaker market fundamentals and on-going biofuel and trade policy uncertainty.

**Targeted Actions to Deliver Cost Savings**

The Company announced today targeted actions to deliver between $500 - $750 million in cost savings over the next 3 - 5 years. These proactive actions will further reduce the Company's costs in response to ongoing market challenges, including global legislative and regulatory policy uncertainty. Specifically, ADM expects to achieve the majority of the cost savings on an annual run-rate basis through improvement in manufacturing costs, reduction in purchased materials and services, and targeted workforce reduction. The Company currently expects a targeted workforce reduction of approximately 600 - 700 roles globally in 2025.

**Dividend**

ADM’s Board of Directors has declared a cash dividend of $51.0 cents per share, up from $50.0 cents per share, on the company’s common stock. The dividend is payable on March 11, 2025 to shareholders of record on February 18, 2025. This is ADM’s 93rd consecutive year of uninterrupted dividends.

**Non-GAAP Financial Measures**

The Company uses certain “Non-GAAP” financial measures as defined by the Securities and Exchange Commission. These are measures of performance not defined by accounting principles generally accepted in the United States, and should be considered in addition to, not in lieu of, GAAP reported measures. Reconciliations of these non-GAAP financial measures to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures are included in this press release.

Adjusted net earnings and Adjusted earnings per share (EPS). Adjusted net earnings reflects ADM’s reported net earnings after removal of the effect on net earnings of specified items as more fully described in the reconciliation tables below. Adjusted EPS reflects ADM’s fully diluted EPS after removal of the effect on EPS as reported of specified items as more fully described in the reconciliation tables below. Management believes that Adjusted net earnings and Adjusted EPS are useful measures of ADM’s performance because they provide investors additional information about ADM’s operations allowing better evaluation of underlying business performance and better period-to-period comparability. These non-GAAP financial measures are not intended to replace or be alternatives to net earnings and EPS as reported, the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures, or any other measures of operating results under GAAP. Earnings amounts described above have been divided by the company’s diluted shares outstanding for each respective period in order to arrive at an adjusted EPS amount for each specified item.

Total segment operating profit. Total segment operating profit is ADM’s consolidated earnings before income taxes adjusted for Other business, Corporate, and specified items as more fully described in the reconciliation tables below. Management believes that total segment operating profit is a useful measure of ADM’s performance because it provides investors information about ADM’s reportable segment performance excluding other business, corporate overhead costs as well as specified items. Total segment operating profit is not a measure of consolidated operating results under U.S. GAAP and should not be considered an alternative to earnings before income taxes, the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure, or any other measure of consolidated operating results under U.S. GAAP.

Adjusted Return on Invested Capital (ROIC). Adjusted ROIC is Adjusted ROIC earnings divided by adjusted invested capital. Adjusted ROIC earnings is ADM’s net earnings adjusted for the after-tax effects of interest expense on borrowings and specified items. Adjusted invested capital is the sum of ADM’s equity (excluding redeemable and non-redeemable noncontrolling interests) and interest-bearing liabilities (which totals invested capital), adjusted for specified items. Management believes Adjusted ROIC is a useful financial measure because it provides investors information about ADM’s returns excluding the impacts of specified items and increases period-to-period comparability of underlying business performance. Management uses Adjusted ROIC to measure ADM’s performance by comparing Adjusted ROIC to its weighted average cost of capital (WACC). Adjusted ROIC, Adjusted ROIC earnings and Adjusted invested capital are non-GAAP financial measures and are not intended to replace or be alternatives to GAAP financial measures.

EBITDA is defined as earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA is defined as earnings before interest on borrowings, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, adjusted for specified items. The Company calculates adjusted EBITDA by removing the impact of specified items and adding back the amounts of income tax expense, interest expense on borrowings, and depreciation and amortization to net earnings. Management believes that EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA are useful measures of the Company’s performance because they provide investors additional information about the Company’s operations allowing better evaluation of underlying business performance and better period-to-period comparability. EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA are non-GAAP financial measures and are not intended to replace or be an alternative to net earnings, the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure.

Cash flows from operations before working capital is defined as cash flows from operating activities excluding the changes in operating assets and liabilities as presented in the Company’s consolidated statement of cash flows. Management believes that cash flows from operations before working capital is a useful measure of the Company’s cash generation. Cash flows from operations before working capital is a non-GAAP financial measure and is not intended to replace or be an alternative to cash from operating activities, the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure.

# ADM Reports Third Quarter 2025 Results and Revises Full-Year Outlook

* by [Madison Hong](https://igrownews.com/author/madison/ "Posts by Madison Hong")
* 5th November 2025

Image provided by ADM.

## Key Takeaways:

* ADM reported third quarter earnings of $108 million, with adjusted net earnings of $448 million.
* Adjusted EPS for the quarter was $0.92, down 16% year-over-year.
* Total segment operating profit reached $845 million, with Nutrition showing 24% growth.
* Year-to-date cash flows from operations totaled $5.8 billion.
* ADM revised its full-year 2025 adjusted EPS guidance to $3.25–$3.50 due to lower crush margins.

---

## ADM Announces Third Quarter 2025 Financial Results

ADM ([NYSE: ADM](https://igrownews.com/agriculture-stocks-performance/)) reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, citing steady progress across core business segments despite a challenging market environment. The company achieved third quarter earnings of $108 million and adjusted net earnings of $448 million. Adjusted earnings per share were $0.92, compared to $1.09 in the same period of 2024.

Chair and CEO [Juan Luciano](https://www.adm.com/en-us/about-adm/our-company/leadership/juan-r.-luciano/) commented, “During the third quarter, we made solid progress in areas within our control, as we navigated a highly dynamic global environment. We advanced our portfolio optimization initiatives, accomplished cost savings through targeted streamlining, efficiently ran our plants, and generated robust cash flow.”

---

## Segment Performance Overview

Total segment operating profit reached $845 million for the third quarter, down 19% year-over-year. ADM’s Ag Services & Oilseeds (AS&O) segment reported $379 million in operating profit, reflecting strong performance in North American exports but lower margins in crushing due to muted biofuel demand and trade challenges.

Carbohydrate Solutions delivered $336 million in segment operating profit, down 26% from the prior year, driven by weaker starches and sweeteners demand and persistent higher corn costs in EMEA. However, the Vantage Corn Processors subsegment benefited from higher ethanol margins and strong export activity.

The Nutrition segment was a bright spot, delivering $130 million in operating profit—a 24% increase over the prior year. Human Nutrition saw double-digit growth, led by record Flavors revenue in North America, while Animal Nutrition rose 79% due to stronger margins and continued portfolio optimization.

---

## Cash Flow, Operations, and Balance Sheet Strength

ADM generated $5.8 billion in cash flows from operating activities year-to-date and reported $2.1 billion in cash flows from operations before working capital adjustments. Luciano highlighted improved inventory management and record volume performance within Ag Services & Oilseeds as key drivers of operational cash flow.

The company continues to emphasize disciplined cost management and portfolio optimization while maintaining a strong liquidity position. Corporate and other business expenses decreased year-over-year, reflecting lower net interest and select corporate costs, excluding specified impairment charges.

---

## Updated 2025 Outlook

ADM revised its adjusted EPS guidance for full-year 2025 to a range of $3.25 to $3.50 per share, down from the prior estimate of approximately $4.00. The company attributed this adjustment primarily to lower global crush margins and deferred biofuel policy impacts.

Luciano stated, “We expect biofuel policy clarity and trade policy evolution to provide demand signals for our industry. However, based on the environment since our last earnings call, we are revising our 2025 full-year expectations primarily to reflect lower crush margins. We are a company built to endure cycles, and our asset network and skilled workforce will remain a source of reliable strength.”

ADM reaffirmed its confidence in its long-term strategy, emphasizing operational efficiency, portfolio balance, and continued investment in sustainable food, feed, and fuel solutions.

### ADM Reports Third Quarter 2025 Results

November 4, 2025

_Third quarter earnings supported by strong business execution and advancement of self-help agenda_

_Robust cash flow supported by portfolio optimization and continued working capital improvement_

_Revised guidance for full-year 2025 based on current biofuel demand environment_

_Expectations of clarity on biofuel policy and global trade evolution underpin constructive outlook for 2026_

CHICAGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--  ADM (NYSE: ADM) today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2025.

**Key Takeaways:**

*   Third quarter earnings of $108 million, with adjusted net earnings 1  of $448 million
*   Third quarter EPS 2  of $0.22, with adjusted EPS 1,2 of $0.92
*   Year-to-date cash flows provided by operating activities were $5.8 billion, with cash flows from operations before working capital 1,3  of $2.1 billion

**Outlook**4**:**

*   Outlook based on performance throughout first nine months of 2025 and current expectations with respect to the timing of anticipated benefits from favorable biofuel policy and global trade evolution
*   Revised previously provided adjusted EPS 1,2  guidance for full-year 2025 to $3.25 - $3.50 per share from approximately $4.00 per share

“During the third quarter, we made solid progress in areas within our control, as we navigated a highly dynamic global environment. We advanced our portfolio optimization initiatives, accomplished cost savings through targeted streamlining, efficiently ran our plants, and generated robust cash flow,” said Chair of the Board and CEO Juan Luciano.

“In AS&O, we achieved several volume records and sharpened our inventory management, both contributing to our overall cash flow. In Carbohydrate Solutions, we delivered another sequentially steady quarter, with uplift from improved ethanol margins. In Nutrition, we achieved sequential growth in operating profit, with record revenue achieved in Flavors North America.

Looking forward, we expect biofuel policy clarity and trade policy evolution to provide demand signals for our industry. However, based on the environment since our last earnings call, we are revising our 2025 full-year expectations primarily to reflect lower crush margins. We are a company built to endure cycles, and our asset network, combined with our skilled workforce, will remain a source of reliable strength for our farmers, customers, partners and investors.”

**Summary of Third Quarter 2025 and Year-to-Date**

For the third quarter ended September 30, 2025, earnings before income taxes were $147 million, as compared to prior year quarter of $108 million. EPS 2 on a GAAP basis was $0.22, as compared to prior year quarter of $0.04. Adjusted EPS 1,2 was $0.92, down 16% versus the prior year quarter of $1.09.

Total segment operating profit 1 was $845 million, down 19% versus the prior year quarter. This excludes specified items of $220 million, which were primarily comprised of portfolio optimization and impairment charges, as well as ADM’s portion of a penalty imposed on Wilmar International Limited (“Wilmar”), a company in which ADM has an equity investment.

Earnings before income taxes were $779 million year-to-date in 2025, down 51% versus the prior year period. EPS 2 on a GAAP basis was $1.29, down 48% versus the prior year period, and adjusted EPS 1,2 was $2.56, down 29% versus the prior year period. Total segment operating profit 1 was $2,422 million year-to-date in 2025, down 23% versus the prior year period.

**Agriculture Services and Oilseeds Summary (AS&O)**

AS&O segment operating profit was $379 million during the third quarter of 2025, down 21% compared to the prior year quarter.

Ag Services subsegment operating profit was 78% higher versus the prior year quarter, driven primarily by higher export activity in North America. In addition, results for South America improved as the prior year quarter was negatively impacted by higher costs related to industry-wide logistics take-or-pay contracts. There were approximately $4 million of net positive mark-to-market timing impacts during the quarter, compared to approximately $50 million of net negative impacts in the prior year quarter.

Crushing subsegment operating profit was 93% lower versus the prior year quarter, driven by lower margins as a result of muted demand due to the deferral of U.S. biofuel policy and challenges with international trade flows. The company has focused on optimizing its operations, and as a result, global crush volumes increased by 2.6% sequentially and 2.2% as compared to the prior year quarter. There were approximately $41 million of net positive mark-to-market timing impacts during the quarter, compared to approximately zero of net impacts in the prior year quarter. Additionally, the prior year quarter benefited from $24 million of insurance proceeds.

Refined Products and Other subsegment operating profit was 3% lower versus the prior year quarter, primarily due to biodiesel and refining margins being negatively impacted by deferred biofuel policy, which has restrained North American demand. There were approximately $8 million of net negative mark-to-market timing impacts during the quarter, compared to approximately $20 million of net negative impacts in the prior year quarter.

Equity earnings from the company’s investment in Wilmar were approximately 10% lower versus the prior year quarter and exclude the $163 million penalty charge, which has been treated as a specified item.

**Carbohydrate Solutions Summary**

Carbohydrate Solutions segment operating profit was $336 million during the third quarter of 2025, down 26% compared to the prior year quarter.

Starches and Sweeteners (S&S) subsegment operating profit decreased by 36% versus the prior year quarter, primarily due to lower global S&S demand, which impacted both volumes and margins. S&S margins continued to be impacted by persisting higher corn costs in EMEA related to corn quality issues. Global wheat milling margins and volumes were fairly stable relative to the prior year quarter. Additionally, the prior year quarter benefited from $47 million of insurance proceeds.

Vantage Corn Processors subsegment operating profit increased by $46 million versus the prior year quarter. Strong export flows during the quarter, coupled with industry inventory dropping as a result of plant downtime related to annual maintenance programs, supported elevated pricing.

**Nutrition Summary**

Nutrition segment operating profit was $130 million during the third quarter of 2025, a 24% increase compared to the prior year quarter.

Human Nutrition subsegment operating profit was 12% higher versus the prior year quarter. In Flavors, operating profit increased, driven largely by higher margins, primarily in North America. In Health & Wellness, operating profit was higher due to increased demand in biotics.

Animal Nutrition subsegment operating profit was up 79% versus the prior year quarter, driven by improved margins as a result of focusing on higher-margin product lines and on-going portfolio streamlining and cost optimization efforts.

**About ADM**

ADM unlocks the power of nature to enrich the quality of life. We’re an essential global agricultural supply chain manager and processor, providing food security by connecting local needs with global capabilities. We’re a premier human and animal nutrition provider, offering one of the industry’s broadest portfolios of ingredients and solutions from nature. We’re a trailblazer in health and well-being, with an industry-leading range of products for consumers looking for new ways to live healthier lives. We’re a cutting-edge innovator, guiding the way to a future of new bio-based consumer and industrial solutions. And we're leading in business-driven sustainability efforts that support a strong agricultural sector, resilient supply chains, and a vast and growing bioeconomy. Around the globe, our expertise and innovation are meeting critical needs from harvest to home. **Non-GAAP Financial Measures**

The Company uses certain “Non-GAAP” financial measures as defined by the Securities and Exchange Commission. These are measures of performance not defined by accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (GAAP), and should be considered in addition to, not in lieu of, GAAP reported measures. Reconciliations of these non-GAAP financial measures to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures are included in this press release.

Adjusted net earnings and Adjusted earnings per share (EPS). Adjusted net earnings reflects ADM’s reported net earnings after removal of the effect on net earnings of specified items as more fully described in the reconciliation tables below. Adjusted EPS reflects ADM’s diluted EPS after removal of the effect on EPS as reported of specified items as more fully described in the reconciliation tables below. Management believes that Adjusted net earnings and Adjusted EPS are useful measures of ADM’s performance because they provide investors additional information about ADM’s operations allowing better evaluation of underlying business performance and better period-to-period comparability. These non-GAAP financial measures are not intended to replace or be alternatives to net earnings and EPS as reported, the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures, or any other measures of operating results under GAAP. Earnings amounts described above have been divided by the company’s diluted shares outstanding for each respective period in order to arrive at an adjusted EPS amount for each specified item.

Total segment operating profit. Total segment operating profit is ADM’s consolidated earnings before income taxes adjusted for Other Business, Corporate, and specified items as more fully described in the reconciliation tables below. Management believes that total segment operating profit is a useful measure of ADM’s performance because it provides investors information about ADM’s reportable segment performance excluding Other Business, Corporate overhead costs as well as specified items. Total segment operating profit is not a measure of consolidated operating results under GAAP and should not be considered an alternative to earnings before income taxes, the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure, or any other measure of consolidated operating results under GAAP.

Adjusted Return on Invested Capital (ROIC). Adjusted ROIC is Adjusted ROIC earnings divided by adjusted invested capital. Adjusted ROIC earnings is ADM’s net earnings adjusted for the after-tax effects of interest expense on borrowings and specified items. Adjusted invested capital is the sum of ADM’s equity (excluding redeemable and non-redeemable non-controlling interests) and interest-bearing liabilities (which totals invested capital), adjusted for specified items. Management believes Adjusted ROIC is a useful financial measure because it provides investors information about ADM’s returns excluding the impacts of specified items and increases period-to-period comparability of underlying business performance. Management uses Adjusted ROIC to measure ADM’s performance by comparing Adjusted ROIC to its weighted average cost of capital (WACC). Adjusted ROIC, Adjusted ROIC earnings and Adjusted invested capital are non-GAAP financial measures and are not intended to replace or be alternatives to GAAP financial measures.

EBITDA is defined as earnings before interest on borrowings, taxes, depreciation and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA is defined as earnings before interest on borrowings, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, adjusted for specified items. The Company calculates Adjusted EBITDA by removing the impact of specified items and adding back the amounts of income tax expense, interest expense on borrowings, and depreciation and amortization to net earnings. Management believes that EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA are useful measures of the Company’s performance because they provide investors additional information about the Company’s operations allowing better evaluation of underlying business performance and better period-to-period comparability. EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA are non-GAAP financial measures and are not intended to replace or be an alternative to net earnings, the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure.

Cash flows from operations before working capital is defined as cash flows from operating activities adjusted for changes in operating assets and liabilities as presented in the Company’s consolidated statement of cash flows. Management believes that cash flows from operations before working capital is a useful measure of the Company’s cash generation. Cash flows from operations before working capital is a non-GAAP financial measure and is not intended to replace or be an alternative to cash from operating activities, the most directly comparable GAAP financial measure.

# Archer-Daniels-Midland Bolsters Shareholder Confidence with Sustained Dividend Payouts

By: [MarketMinute](https://markets.financialcontent.com/wral/news/provider/marketminute)

October 21, 2025 at 17:04 PM EDT

**Decatur, IL – October 21, 2025** – Archer-Daniels-Midland Company ([NYSE: ADM](https://markets.financialcontent.com/wral/quote?Symbol=NY%3AADM)), a global leader in human and animal nutrition and the world's premier agricultural origination and processing company, has consistently demonstrated its commitment to shareholder returns by maintaining a quarterly dividend of $0.50 per share. This steadfast approach to dividend distribution, which saw an increase from $0.45 to $0.50 per share in early 2024, underscores the company's robust financial health and management's confidence in its long-term earnings potential. For the broader food processing industry, ADM's sustained dividend performance serves as a powerful indicator of stability and resilience within a sector crucial to global sustenance.

The consistent declaration of a competitive dividend not only enhances ADM's appeal to income-focused investors but also reinforces its reputation as a reliable "Dividend Aristocrat," a testament to over three decades of increasing dividend payouts. This strategy highlights ADM's effective operational management and ability to generate substantial cash flow, even amidst dynamic market conditions. In an industry often subject to commodity price volatility and supply chain disruptions, ADM's predictable shareholder returns signal a strong underlying business model and a strategic focus on delivering consistent value.

## A Legacy of Returns: ADM's Dividend Strategy Unpacked

Archer-Daniels-Midland Company's journey to its current $0.50 quarterly dividend per share is rooted in a long-standing commitment to shareholder value. The initial declaration of the increased dividend to $0.50 per share occurred on January 25, 2024, marking an approximate 11% hike from the previous $0.45 per share. This dividend was subsequently paid on February 29, 2024, to shareholders of record as of February 8, 2024. Following this, ADM continued its consistent payout, declaring the same $0.50 dividend on August 7, 2024, payable on September 11, 2024, and again on November 8, 2024, payable on December 12, 2024. These declarations underscore a stable and predictable pattern of returning capital to investors.

The key players involved in this decision-making process include ADM's Board of Directors, who approve the dividend declarations, and the executive leadership team responsible for the financial performance that supports such payouts. Shareholders, particularly those focused on income and long-term value, are the primary stakeholders who directly benefit. The immediate market reaction to these declarations has generally been positive, reinforcing investor confidence in ADM's financial stability and its ability to generate consistent free cash flow. This consistency is particularly noteworthy given the global economic landscape and the inherent volatility in agricultural markets. ADM's track record of 369 consecutive quarterly payments by January 2024, extending over 92 years, and 372 by November 2024, spanning 93 years, speaks volumes about its enduring financial strength and disciplined capital allocation. This impressive history solidifies its status as a cornerstone investment for those seeking stability and growth in their portfolios.

## Impact on the Food Processing Landscape: Winners and Losers

Archer-Daniels-Midland ([NYSE: ADM](https://markets.financialcontent.com/wral/quote?Symbol=NY%3AADM))'s consistent and increasing dividend policy positions the company as a clear winner in the eyes of investors, particularly those seeking stable income and long-term growth. The company's robust financial health, evidenced by a sustainable dividend payout ratio of approximately 30% (significantly below the sector median of 48%), allows it to attract and retain a loyal shareholder base. This strong financial footing enables ADM to continue investing in strategic growth areas, such as its nutrition business and sustainable solutions, further cementing its market leadership. By demonstrating consistent profitability and a commitment to shareholder returns, ADM enhances its brand and market perception, potentially leading to a lower cost of capital and greater flexibility for future expansion or acquisitions.

In the broader food processing industry, ADM's performance can serve as a benchmark. Companies with similar business models or those aspiring to ADM's level of financial stability might find themselves pressured to demonstrate comparable returns to shareholders. This could lead to a competitive environment where companies are incentivized to optimize their operations, improve efficiency, and enhance profitability to support their own dividend policies. While direct "losers" are not immediately apparent from ADM's dividend declaration, smaller or less financially robust companies in the sector might struggle to match ADM's consistent dividend growth, potentially making their stocks less attractive to income-focused investors. This disparity could lead to a widening gap in investor appeal and market capitalization between industry leaders like ADM and their smaller counterparts.

Furthermore, ADM's ability to sustain and grow its dividend, partly attributed to its capacity to navigate and potentially benefit from "basic food inflation," suggests a resilient business model that can pass on costs. This dynamic could place pressure on other food processors who lack similar market power or diversified revenue streams, potentially impacting their margins and, consequently, their ability to reward shareholders. For consumers, while not directly impacted by the dividend itself, the underlying strength that allows ADM to maintain its dividend could translate into continued investment in product innovation and supply chain efficiency, ultimately benefiting the end-user through a stable and diverse food supply.

## Broader Significance: Industry Trends and Ripple Effects

ADM's sustained dividend performance is more than just a corporate financial decision; it's a significant indicator of broader trends within the agricultural and food processing industry. In an era marked by increasing global food demand, supply chain complexities, and a growing emphasis on sustainable practices, ADM's ability to consistently generate strong cash flow and reward shareholders speaks to the fundamental strength and essential nature of its business. This event fits into the broader trend of large, diversified agricultural companies leveraging their scale and integrated operations to navigate market volatility and deliver stable financial results. It highlights the importance of robust risk management, diversified product portfolios (from agricultural origination to specialty ingredients), and efficient global logistics in maintaining profitability.

The ripple effects of ADM's dividend stability extend to its competitors and partners. For competitors like Bunge Limited ([NYSE: BG](https://markets.financialcontent.com/wral/quote?Symbol=NY%3ABG)) and Cargill (private), ADM's strong shareholder returns set a high bar for financial performance and capital allocation. While Cargill is privately held, Bunge's dividend policies and overall financial health are often viewed in comparison to ADM. Such consistent payouts from a major player can influence investor expectations across the sector, encouraging other publicly traded companies to prioritize shareholder returns where feasible. For partners, including farmers, suppliers, and customers, ADM's financial strength ensures a reliable and stable partner, fostering long-term relationships and contributing to the overall stability of the agricultural value chain. Regulatory bodies also take note of such financial indicators, as the health of major food processors like ADM is critical for food security and market stability. There are no immediate direct regulatory or policy implications from a dividend declaration itself, but the underlying financial strength it represents can influence broader discussions around agricultural policy, trade, and sustainability initiatives. Historically, consistent dividend payers in essential industries have often been seen as pillars of economic stability, and ADM's performance reinforces this perception.

## What Comes Next: Navigating Future Market Dynamics

Looking ahead, Archer-Daniels-Midland ([NYSE: ADM](https://markets.financialcontent.com/wral/quote?Symbol=NY%3AADM))'s continued commitment to a strong dividend payout signals several short-term and long-term possibilities for the company and the broader market. In the short term, investors can likely expect continued stability in ADM's dividend, reinforcing its position as a reliable income stock. This predictability can attract further investment from institutional and retail investors seeking defensive assets in an uncertain economic climate. For ADM, this stability provides a solid foundation for strategic pivots. The company is likely to continue its focus on high-growth areas such as its nutrition segment, which offers higher margins and diversification away from purely commodity-driven businesses. Investments in sustainable solutions and bio-based products are also anticipated, aligning with global environmental trends and consumer preferences.

In the long term, ADM's sustained financial health, as evidenced by its dividend, positions it to capitalize on emerging market opportunities and navigate potential challenges. The increasing global population and evolving dietary patterns will continue to drive demand for ADM's products and services. However, challenges such as climate change impacts on crop yields, geopolitical tensions affecting trade routes, and increasing regulatory scrutiny on food production practices will require continuous adaptation. ADM's robust cash flow provides the flexibility to invest in research and development for climate-resilient crops, advanced processing technologies, and efficient supply chain management to mitigate these risks. Potential scenarios include further strategic acquisitions in the nutrition or sustainable materials space, continued expansion into developing markets, and ongoing optimization of its core agricultural services. Market opportunities may arise from technological advancements in precision agriculture and biotechnology, which ADM is well-positioned to integrate into its operations.

## Comprehensive Wrap-Up: A Pillar of Stability in a Dynamic Market

Archer-Daniels-Midland Company's ([NYSE: ADM](https://markets.financialcontent.com/wral/quote?Symbol=NY%3AADM)) consistent declaration and increase of its quarterly dividend to $0.50 per share stands as a testament to its enduring financial strength and strategic foresight within the critical food processing industry. The key takeaway from this event is ADM's unwavering commitment to delivering shareholder value, backed by robust operational performance and a sustainable business model. This commitment not only solidifies its status as a "Dividend Aristocrat" but also enhances its appeal to a broad spectrum of investors seeking both income and stability.

Moving forward, the market can view ADM as a reliable anchor in the often-volatile agricultural and food sectors. Its ability to maintain and grow dividends, even amidst global economic shifts and commodity price fluctuations, underscores the defensive characteristics of the food processing industry and ADM's leadership within it. Investors should closely watch for ADM's continued investments in its nutrition segment and sustainable initiatives, as these areas are poised to drive future growth and further diversify its revenue streams. The company's capacity to navigate inflationary pressures and adapt to evolving consumer demands will also be crucial indicators of its ongoing success. Ultimately, ADM's dividend strategy reflects a company that is not only financially sound but also strategically positioned to thrive in the complex global food ecosystem for years to come, making it a compelling consideration for long-term portfolio stability.

Archer joined the firm. Archer-Daniels-Midland Company is a leading producer of various [food and beverage](https://market.us/statistics/food-and-beverage-companies/) ingredients, and products made used in the agricultural sector. The company operates through four segments namely: Oilseeds, Origination, Nutrition, and Carbohydrate Solutions. This company offers various products such as natural colors and flavors, nutrition and health products, corn sweeteners, vegetable oils, flour, biofuels, and animal feed. The company has an extensive range of global grain elevators and transportation networks in order to procure, clean, store, and transport agricultural products such as oilseeds, wheat, corn, milo, barley, and oats, as well as various derived products.

The company’s growth strategy is spread across five key growth platforms: Nutrition, Taste, Animal Nutrition, Carbohydrates, and Health and Wellness. The company also engages in agricultural commodities, handling and merchandising activities, activities associated with structured trade finance, and distribution and import of different agricultural feed products. This company offers protein meals and vegetable oils, ingredients for food, energy, feed, and different industrial products industries, salad oils, crude vegetable oils, shortening, margarine, and other food products; and refined oils in order to produce glycols and biodiesel for applications in paints, chemicals, and other industrial products.

The company offers peanuts, peanut-derived ingredients, tree nuts, cotton cellulose pulp, and cottonseed flour; sweeteners, wheat and corn starches, glucose, dextrose, syrup, and various other bioproducts; animal and food feed ingredients; and alcohol, ethanol, and ethyl alcohol; corn gluten meal and feed; and citric acids. In addition, the company offers natural flavor ingredients, natural colors, flavor systems, proteins, soluble fibers, emulsifiers, polyols, nutrition, and natural health products, hydrocolloids, and various other specialty feed and food ingredients; formula feeds, and animal nutrition and health products; edible beans; and private and contract label pet foods and treats. The company is also engaged in futures insurance and commission merchant services.

## **Financial Highlights:**

* The company’s overall revenue increased from US$ 64,656 Million in 2019 to US$ 64,355 Million in 2020.
* The company’s Ag Services and Oilseeds segment’s overall revenue decreased from US$ 54,633 Million in 2019 to US$ 49,716 Million in 2020.
* The company’s carbohydrate solutions segment’s overall revenue decreased from US$ 11,154 Million in 2019 to US$ 8,472 Million in 2020.
* The company’s nutrition segment’s overall revenue increased from US$ 5,786 Million in 2019 to US$ 2,812 Million in 2020.

## **Business Strategy:**

The company’s growth strategies are spread across five key growth platforms: Nutrition, Taste, Animal Nutrition, Carbohydrates, and Health and Wellness. The company is committed to executing these strategies and this vision by conducting business in accordance with core values of treating others with respect, operating with integrity, achieving excellence, displaying teamwork, being responsible, and being resourceful.

A company uses/employs its significant asset base to transport and originate agricultural commodities and connect to markets in more than 170 countries. The company processes oilseeds, corn, and wheat into products for animal feed, food, energy, and chemical uses. This company is engaged in the manufacturing, distribution, and sale of specialty products such as natural flavor ingredients, natural colors, flavor systems, proteins, soluble fiber, emulsifiers, polyols, natural and nutrition products, hydrocolloids, and other specialty food and feed ingredients.

The company’s operations are managed, organized, and classified into four business segments: Oilseeds, Origination, Nutrition, and Carbohydrate Solutions. These segments are organized based on the nature of services and products offered. In addition, other operations are not reportable business segments and are defined by applicable accounting standards.

## **2018 Highlights:**

* In June 2018, the company invested 50% interest in SoyVen, which was a joint venture with Cargill, in order to offer soybean oil and meal consumers in Egypt
* In June 2018, the company acquired 50% shares of Russian-based Aston Foods and Food Ingredients in order to expand its sweeteners and starches business
* In August 2018, the company acquired Probiotics International Limited, which is a UK-based company that offers probiotic supplements for a pet, human, and production animal uses
* In August 2018, the company acquired Rodelle Inc.
* In October 2018, the company established GrainBridge LLC, which is a 50% joint venture with Cargill
* In December 2018, the company acquired Brazil-based Algar Agro, in order to enhance its soybean originations refining, crushing, and bottling assets

## **2019 Highlights:**

* In January 2019, the company acquired Neovia, which is a France-based provider of value-added animal nutrition solutions. Neovia has 72 production facilities and offers services in 25 countries.
* In January 2019, the company signed an agreement to purchase Florida Chemical Company, which is a US-based provider of citrus oils and other ingredients
* In January 2019, the company signed a purchase agreement with Gleadell Agriculture Ltd. in order to secure regulatory approval
* In March, the company acquired Florida Chemical Company.
* In May, the company acquired Ziegler Group, a provider of natural citrus flavor ingredients.

## **2020 Highlights:**

* In January, the company acquired Yerbalatina Phytoactives, a plant-based extracts and ingredients manufacturer.
* In April, the company entered into a partnership with Sazerac to increase hand sanitizer production.
* In May, the company along with [Marfrig Global Foods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marfrig) announced the formation of the joint venture, PlantPlus Foods to deliver plant-based products in South American and North American markets.
* In July, the company launched NutriPass L, an encapsulated lysine supplement.

# Archer-Daniels-Midland: Business Model, SWOT Analysis, and Competitors 2024

## Introduction

Archer-Daniels-Midland Company (ADM) is a global leader in human and animal nutrition and the world’s premier agricultural origination and processing company. Founded in 1902 and headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, ADM has grown into a multi-billion-dollar enterprise that influences global food supply chains. Its operations span continents, engaging in activities that range from the origination of crops to the manufacture of oils, protein meals, and other essential products.

In this comprehensive analysis, we will delve into ADM's business model, conduct a SWOT analysis to identify its strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats, and identify key competitors that ADM will face in 2024.

## What You Will Learn

1. **ADM's Business Model:** Understanding the core elements of ADM’s business strategy and operations.
2. **SWOT Analysis:** A detailed examination of ADM’s internal strengths and weaknesses, as well as external opportunities and threats.
3. **Competitors in 2024:** Insight into the key players in the agribusiness and food processing industry that compete with ADM.
4. **Key Takeaways:** Summarizing the essential points from the analysis.
5. **FAQs:** Addressing common questions about ADM.

## Key Takeaways

* ADM is a global leader in agricultural origination and processing.
* The company has a diversified business model with significant investments in innovation and sustainability.
* ADM faces competition from other giants in the industry like Cargill, Bunge, and Louis Dreyfus Company (LDC).
* The SWOT analysis reveals ADM’s strategic advantages and areas that need attention, including market expansion and technological advancements.

## ADM's Business Model

ADM’s business model is multifaceted, encompassing a wide array of operations within the agricultural supply chain. Here’s an in-depth look at the core elements:

### 1. **Origination**

ADM sources crops such as corn, wheat, soybeans, and other grains from farmers around the globe. The company works closely with agricultural producers to ensure a consistent supply of raw materials. This step involves not only procurement but also logistics management to transport these crops to various processing facilities.

### 2. **Processing**

Once the raw materials are sourced, ADM processes them into a variety of products. The processing segment includes:

* **Oilseeds Processing:** Crushing oilseeds to produce vegetable oils and protein meals.
* **Corn Processing:** Converting corn into sweeteners, starches, and bio-products like ethanol.
* **Wheat Milling:** Producing flour and other wheat-based products.

### 3. **Nutrition**

This segment focuses on producing ingredients for human and animal nutrition. ADM manufactures products such as:

* **Human Nutrition:** Plant-based proteins, natural flavors, and health and wellness products.
* **Animal Nutrition:** Feed ingredients, premixes, and specialty feed solutions for livestock.

### 4. **Distribution**

ADM operates a vast network of transportation and storage facilities, ensuring efficient distribution of its products. The company’s extensive logistics capabilities include:

* **Shipping:** Operating a fleet of vessels for ocean transport.
* **Storage:** Managing a global network of silos and warehouses.

### 5. **Innovation and Sustainability**

ADM invests heavily in research and development to innovate its product offerings and improve process efficiencies. The company is also committed to sustainability, focusing on reducing its carbon footprint, promoting responsible sourcing, and enhancing food security.

## SWOT Analysis

A SWOT analysis helps to identify the internal and external factors that affect ADM's performance:

### Strengths

1. **Global Presence:** ADM operates in over 170 countries, giving it a vast market reach and diversified revenue streams.
2. **Integrated Supply Chain:** The company’s end-to-end supply chain capabilities ensure efficiency and cost-effectiveness.
3. **Innovative R&D:** ADM’s investment in research and development fosters innovation in product offerings and process improvements.
4. **Strong Brand Reputation:** With over a century of experience, ADM is a trusted name in the agribusiness sector.

### Weaknesses

1. **Dependence on Agricultural Commodities:** ADM’s profitability is highly influenced by the volatility of agricultural commodity prices.
2. **High Operating Costs:** The extensive global operations and logistics network contribute to significant operating expenses.
3. **Regulatory Risks:** The company operates in a highly regulated industry, with exposure to changing policies and trade regulations.

### Opportunities

1. **Market Expansion:** Growing demand for plant-based proteins and health-focused food products presents opportunities for market expansion.
2. **Technological Advancements:** Innovations in biotechnology and digital agriculture can enhance productivity and reduce costs.
3. **Sustainability Initiatives:** Increasing consumer and regulatory focus on sustainability offers opportunities for ADM to lead in sustainable agribusiness practices.

### Threats

1. **Intense Competition:** ADM faces stiff competition from other major players in the agribusiness sector.
2. **Climate Change:** Adverse weather conditions and climate change can impact crop yields and supply chain stability.
3. **Geopolitical Risks:** Political instability and trade tensions in key markets can disrupt operations and supply chains.

## Competitors in 2024

The agribusiness and food processing industry is highly competitive. Here are some of the key competitors ADM will face in 2024:

### 1. **Cargill**

Cargill is one of the largest privately held companies in the United States, with a diverse range of operations in agriculture, food, and industrial products. Like ADM, Cargill has a global footprint and a strong focus on innovation and sustainability.

### 2. **Bunge Limited**

Bunge is a leading global agribusiness and food company, specializing in oilseed processing, grain trading, and food production. The company’s extensive network of facilities and strong market presence make it a formidable competitor.

### 3. **Louis Dreyfus Company (LDC)**

LDC is a global merchant and processor of agricultural goods, operating in over 100 countries. The company’s diversified portfolio includes grains, oilseeds, coffee, cotton, and sugar. LDC’s strong supply chain capabilities and focus on sustainability position it as a key competitor to ADM.

### 4. **Tyson Foods**

Tyson Foods is a major player in the food industry, particularly in meat processing. While not a direct competitor in all segments, Tyson’s focus on protein production and its expanding portfolio of plant-based products make it a significant competitor in the nutrition space.

### 5. **Nestlé**

Nestlé is the world’s largest food and beverage company, with a diverse range of products and a strong global presence. The company’s focus on nutrition, health, and wellness aligns with ADM’s strategic goals, making it a key competitor in the human nutrition segment.

## Conclusion

Archer-Daniels-Midland Company stands as a global leader in the agribusiness sector, leveraging its extensive supply chain capabilities, innovative R&D, and commitment to sustainability. The SWOT analysis highlights ADM's strengths, such as its global presence and integrated supply chain, while also identifying areas for improvement, such as managing commodity price volatility and regulatory risks.

In 2024, ADM will face competition from major players like Cargill, Bunge, LDC, Tyson Foods, and Nestlé. However, the company's strategic focus on market expansion, technological advancements, and sustainability initiatives positions it well for continued growth and leadership in the industry.

## FAQs

### 1. **What does ADM do?**

ADM is a global leader in agricultural origination and processing, producing a wide range of products for human and animal nutrition. The company sources crops, processes them into oils, protein meals, and other products, and distributes them globally.

### 2. **Who are ADM’s main competitors?**

ADM’s main competitors include Cargill, Bunge, Louis Dreyfus Company, Tyson Foods, and Nestlé. These companies compete with ADM in various segments of the agribusiness and food processing industry.

### 3. **What are ADM’s strengths?**

ADM’s strengths include its global presence, integrated supply chain, innovative R&D, and strong brand reputation. These factors contribute to the company’s leadership in the agribusiness sector.

### 4. **What are some opportunities for ADM?**

Opportunities for ADM include market expansion in plant-based proteins and health-focused food products, technological advancements in biotechnology and digital agriculture, and leading in sustainable agribusiness practices.

### 5. **What challenges does ADM face?**

ADM faces challenges such as commodity price volatility, high operating costs, regulatory risks, intense competition, climate change, and geopolitical risks. Managing these challenges is crucial for the company’s continued success.

### 6. **How does ADM ensure sustainability?**

ADM is committed to sustainability through initiatives aimed at reducing its carbon footprint, promoting responsible sourcing, and enhancing food security. The company invests in sustainable practices and collaborates with stakeholders to achieve its sustainability goals.

# Deep Dive Into the Archer Daniels Midland Company Profile

by Ryan Murray

**Archer-Daniels-Midland Company**  
NYSE: ADM  
77 West Wacker Drive  
Suite 4600  
Chicago, IL 60601  
United States  
Main Phone: (312) 634-8100  
Website: [https://www.adm.com](https://www.adm.com "Archer Daniels Midland website")

## Key Highlights

* ADM, a leader in nutrition, has chosen Juan Luciano as its ninth chief executive. This signals a new time for the company, which has been around for a century.
* The company is working on changing its product range to meet the changing needs of consumers who want sustainable and plant-based options.
* ADM is focusing on being more efficient. It is improving its supply chains, making manufacturing better, and finding ways to cut costs.
* ADM is bringing together functions, cutting down its number of employees, and simplifying what it offers. This will help the company be quicker and more flexible in response to market changes.
* By simplifying its structure, ADM wants to empower its workers, encourage teamwork, and speed up how decisions are made.

## Introduction

Archer Daniels Midland (ADM) is an important name in the global nutrition and animal nutrition business, with a history of leadership including executives like those from Dow Chemical and Kristy Folkwein, as well as connections to successful entities such as PepsiCo. The company has over a century of heritage and remarkable evolution in its history. ADM, based in Illinois, keeps changing to meet the world's changing nutrition needs. The choice of Juan Luciano as the ninth chief executive and a member of the board of directors for Eli Lilly marks an important move. This will help strengthen ADM's role in the food and agriculture industry, which is always changing.

## ADM's Strategic Growth through Sustainable Solutions

 ADM cares about the environment and knows that more people want eco-friendly products. This is clear in its plan to grow in areas like renewable fuels and plant-based proteins. These efforts are good for the earth and also open up profitable markets that are growing fast.

By putting money into these areas, ADM can use its skills in farming and food processing. This will help them build a stronger and more sustainable business. It also helps the company respond to the changing wishes of customers who are more aware of how their food choices affect the planet.

### Expanding the Core Business with Renewable Fuels and Plant-Based Proteins

ADM is leading the way in sustainable farming. The company is using its skills to enter the renewable fuels market. They know that reducing our need for fossil fuels is important. ADM is dedicated to creating sustainable options. By investing in biofuels, they help the planet and take part in a growing market focused on environmental issues.

Besides renewable fuels, ADM is also moving into the plant-based protein market. More people want healthy and eco-friendly food. This means the demand for plant-based proteins like soy and pea is increasing. ADM's expertise in farming and processing gives them an edge to meet this rising need.

This move into plant-based proteins fits with ADM’s goal of providing sustainable and nutritious food. They offer many plant-based ingredients that keep up with what consumers want. This helps build a better food system while meeting changing dietary choices.

### Leveraging Global Partnerships for Access to New Markets

Global partnerships are very important for ADM's growth. These alliances help the company reach new markets and expand worldwide. A key example is ADM's partnership with Wilmar International, which is a big agribusiness group in Asia.

This partnership has made ADM much stronger in the Asia-Pacific area. This region offers great chances for growth in food and agriculture. By using Wilmar's strong distribution networks and market knowledge, ADM can share its products and services with more consumers.

These global partnerships help ADM enter new markets and gain insights into local consumer choices and market trends. Understanding these trends is key for creating products that meet local needs. This, in turn, boosts growth and makes ADM more competitive in the global market.

## Operational Efficiencies and Cost-Cutting Measures

Operational efficiency is very important for ADM. The company wants to stay ahead of the competition. It is using different methods to improve its operations. Right now, it is focusing on supply chain management and manufacturing processes. By making its supply chains better, ADM can lower transportation costs, speed up delivery times, and boost efficiency.

ADM is also looking closely at its manufacturing processes. They want to find and remove delays, cut down on waste, and raise productivity. ADM is spending money on new technologies and using lean manufacturing methods. This will help them reduce manufacturing costs and make their products more competitive around the world.

### Streamlining Supply Chains and Reducing Manufacturing Costs

ADM knows that a strong and effective supply chain is very important in today’s global economy. To make its operations better, the company is spending on the latest technologies, improving transport routes, and building closer ties with suppliers. These actions help lower transport costs, speed up delivery times, and improve overall efficiency in the supply chain.

In addition, ADM is working on improving its manufacturing processes to boost productivity and cut costs. This means using automation, data analysis, and process upgrades to find and fix issues, waste less, and make production smoother. By doing these things, ADM aims to lower production costs, so its products can compete better in the global market.

Through all these efforts, ADM is making its operations more efficient while also creating a business model that reflects the increased use of sustainable practices and is more cost-effective. This focus on improving continuously helps the company ensure it can provide high-quality products at competitive prices successfully.

### Targeted Workforce Reduction and Portfolio Simplification

In pursuit of heightened operational efficiency, ADM has undertaken strategic workforce reductions. These reductions, while difficult, are designed to streamline the organization, eliminate redundancies, and create a more agile and responsive workforce. This strategic move allows ADM to allocate resources more effectively and focus on its core growth areas.

Alongside workforce adjustments, ADM is simplifying its business portfolio, divesting non-core assets and concentrating on its most promising segments. This simplification aims to sharpen the company's strategic focus, allowing it to direct investments and resources toward areas with the highest growth potential.

| Initiative | Description | Expected Outcome |
| Workforce Reduction | Streamlining workforce to eliminate redundancies and increase agility. | Reduced costs and improved organizational agility |
| Portfolio Simplification | Divesting non-core assets to sharpen strategic focus. | Enhanced profitability and growth potential |

## Organizational Streamlining for Agility and Efficiency

 ADM knows that being flexible is important in today's fast-changing business world. To be more adaptable, ADM is changing its structure. This change means bringing together some functions to remove any overlaps and wastefulness. By grouping similar tasks, ADM can make its processes smoother, improve teamwork, and lower administrative costs.

Moreover, ADM is focusing on building a work environment that is more collaborative and empowering. By removing traditional barriers and encouraging teamwork across different areas, the company hopes to boost creativity. This will help ADM become an organization that can quickly respond to changing market demands and what customers want.

### Centralizing Functions to Eliminate Redundancies

As part of its plan to simplify how it works, ADM is bringing some functions together into one place. This means combining similar tasks that used to be done in different departments or business units. For example, human resources, finance, governance, and IT services are being grouped into shared service centers, leveraging AI technology to enhance efficiency.

The goal of this centralization is to cut out duplicate efforts that happen when different departments do the same job. By combining these functions, ADM can make things work smoother, lower costs, and free up resources for the main business activities.

Also, by centralizing functions, ADM can make processes the same across the company and use the best methods. This helps make everything more efficient and ensures that the quality of services is good, no matter where or which unit is involved.

### Flattening the Hierarchy for Improved Communication

ADM wants to build a more flexible and fast-working organization. They aim to reduce the traditional layered structure. This means empowering all employees, not just those at the top. ADM encourages teamwork and open communication. They want staff to work together and share ideas easily.

With a simpler structure, decisions can be made quicker. There are fewer management layers, which means people at all levels can decide things right where they are needed. This helps ADM respond quickly to market changes and new customer needs.

In addition, a simpler structure makes employees feel more involved and valued. By allowing them more control and responsibility, ADM creates a sense of ownership. This approach helps spark new ideas and creativity, as employees are more willing to share their thoughts and suggestions.

### Who is Juan Luciano, CEO at ADM?

Juan Luciano is the Chairman and CEO of Archer Daniels Midland (ADM), a global leader in agricultural processing and nutrition. He joined ADM in 2011 as Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, and rose to the CEO position in 2015. Under his leadership, ADM has transformed into a global nutrition business, expanding its footprint and focusing on sustainable solutions. 3  Luciano has driven the company's growth through strategic acquisitions, technological innovation, and a commitment to meeting evolving customer needs. 2  Before ADM, he had a successful 25-year career at Dow Chemical.

### Who is Kristy Folkwein, CIO at ADM?

Kristy Folkwein is the Senior Vice President and Chief Information Officer (CIO) at Archer Daniels Midland (ADM), a global leader in agricultural processing and nutrition. She joined ADM in 2016 and is responsible for the company's global IT strategy.  Folkwein leads initiatives focused on data integrity, analytics, and modernizing ADM's technology practices. Her role is crucial in supporting ADM's vast and complex operations, which span over 1,100 locations and 44,000 employees across six continents. Folkwein has extensive experience in IT leadership roles. Before ADM, she served as CIO at Dow Corning and held IT leadership positions at Ashland, Inc.

### Who is Monish Patolawala, CFO at ADM?

Monish Patolawala is the Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) at Archer Daniels Midland (ADM).  Joining ADM in July 2024, he brings over 25 years of financial leadership experience from global industrial and healthcare companies.  At ADM, Patolawala oversees Global Finance and Accounting, Global Business Services, Global Technology, and Enterprise Strategy, and is a member of the Executive Council. Previously, Patolawala was President and CFO of 3M, leading finance, IT, and enterprise strategy.  He also spent over two decades at General Electric (GE), including as CFO of GE Healthcare.  His background includes a chartered accountant certification and a bachelor's degree from St. Joseph's College of Commerce (Bangalore, India).  Patolawala's extensive experience positions him to play a key role in ADM's financial strategy and growth.

## Historical Evolution of ADM

Archer Daniels Midland (ADM) has a rich history that dates back to 1902 when it was founded by George A. Archer and John W. Daniels in Minneapolis, Minnesota. Originally focusing on grain storage and processing, the company expanded its scope in the 1920s by acquiring multiple grain elevators and diversifying into the production of corn and soy-based products. As the demand for food and agriculture-related products increased, ADM capitalized on emerging technologies, introducing innovative processes for extracting oil from seeds and developing high-fructose corn syrup. Throughout the decades, the firm strategically expanded its global footprint through key acquisitions, including the purchase of leading agricultural companies and the establishment of operations in various countries. Today, ADM stands as a leading player in the agribusiness sector, firmly rooted in its foundational principles while continually evolving to meet the changing needs of its customers and the marketplace.

## In-depth Review of ADM’s Business Model

Archer Daniels Midland (ADM) operates with a robust business model that emphasizes both vertical integration and global reach. By controlling various segments of the supply chain, from sourcing raw agricultural products to processing and distributing finished goods, ADM effectively manages its own risk while enhancing profitability. The company's diverse portfolio spans key segments such as agricultural services, oilseeds, corn processing, and nutrition, allowing it to adapt to market fluctuations and capitalize on emerging opportunities. Moreover, ADM’s commitment to sustainability and innovation is reflected through its investments in renewable energy and eco-friendly practices, positioning the company as a leader in the agri-food sector. This comprehensive strategy not only strengthens its market position but also fosters long-term growth and resilience, ensuring that ADM remains a pivotal player in the global agricultural landscape.

## Future Innovations and Strategic Directions

As the Archer Daniels Midland Company continues to evolve in the dynamic landscape of the food and agriculture sector, its future innovations and strategic directions are poised to emphasize sustainability, technological advancement, and global market expansion. The company plans to invest significantly in research and development to pioneer next-generation agricultural practices that not only enhance crop yields but also reduce environmental impact. Furthermore, ADM is exploring advancements in biotechnology and digital agriculture, aiming to integrate smart farming technologies that optimize efficiency from seed to shelf. In addition to these innovations, ADM's strategic direction includes forming strategic partnerships and collaborations with other industry leaders to leverage expertise and resources, ultimately driving growth and maintaining a competitive edge in the market. As consumer preferences shift towards more sustainable and ethically produced food options, ADM remains committed to aligning its business practices with these values, ensuring a resilient and forward-thinking business model for years to come.

## Executive Leadership and Corporate Influence

Archer Daniels Midland (ADM) boasts a dynamic executive leadership team that not only steers the company’s strategic direction but also significantly influences the global agricultural landscape. The leadership, with its wealth of experience across multiple sectors, is committed to driving innovation and sustainability within the food and agriculture industries. Each executive brings a unique perspective, underpinned by a steadfast dedication to ethical business practices and community engagement. By fostering a culture of collaboration and connectivity, ADM's leaders inspire teams to achieve operational excellence and enhance stakeholder relationships. Their visionary approach not only positions ADM as a market leader but also reinforces its commitment to enhancing food security and advancing sustainable farming practices worldwide.

## Conclusion

In conclusion, the Archer Daniels Midland Company focuses on sustainable solutions. This approach helps them work better and adapt to the market. ADM is moving towards renewable fuels and plant-based proteins. They are also forming global partnerships and cutting costs. These actions help build a strong future. Their focus on being quick, efficient, and sustainable benefits the company. It also matches the higher demand for eco-friendly practices today.
